newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 3.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Monday:

* Abortion protestors hoped a bill banning controversial late-term abortions would have a greater chance of becoming law after the head of a pro-abortion lobby admitted last week that he lied when he said such procedures were rarely performed.

* Ian Wilmut, the embryologist who successfully cloned an adult sheep, discussed in an interview the challenges of such a feat. He said the key factor was starvation of adult cells taken from the sheep's progenitor.

* The Albanian government declared a nationwide state of emergency as rebellion and anarchy spread following the collapse of a string of fraudulent investment schemes in which hundreds of Albanians have lost their life savings.
* Vice President Al Gore is getting drawn into the controversy over Democratic fund-raising methods following revelations of his participation in some of these efforts.
* The Central Intelligence Agency has purged more than 100 foreign agents from its payroll after concluding that they were involved in activities such as murder and torture.

* Sweden showed its alarm over the growing membership of American-based gangs there by sending in 300 police officers to control festivities accompanying the opening of a new clubhouse for the Hell's Angels motorcycle gang in Stockholm.

* New York State's unseasonably warm winter has left its municipal and county governments with some unexpected cash, but personal injury lawyers, ski resorts, sanitation workers and certain businesses are feeling the pinch.
